investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official 'Agenda' page and one individual event permalink page, plus a confirmatory unauthenticated GET of this WordPress install's own bundled 'The Events Calendar' plugin REST API.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of the venue's official 'Agenda' page (https://www.sunset-sunside.com/agenda/) already exposes real, server-rendered event cards (<li class="concert ..." data-horaire="YYYYMMDDHHmm">), each with its own title, room name ('Sunset' or 'Sunside'), and a machine-readable full date+time timestamp directly in a data-horaire attribute — already fully answering the investigation question at Level 1. A confirmatory check of this WordPress install's own CSS class names (single-tribe_events on a detail page) led to a plain, unauthenticated GET of its own bundled 'The Events Calendar' plugin REST API (/wp-json/tribe/events/v1/events), which is genuinely public (HTTP 200, no access_token/login/CAPTCHA) and returns an even richer, fully structured JSON record per event — id, title, slug, start_date/end_date with BOTH local and true UTC variants plus an explicit IANA timezone, cost, and a nested venue object stating its own name/address/city/zip. This is the SAME existing, already-generic ingestion/events-calendar-api/ family already proven for ccb-lisbon-01 — zero new collector code required, only a per-source config.

venue_reference: Sunset / Sunside (jazz club, rue des Lombards, Paris 1er — ONE single venue/business with two named performance rooms, 'Sunset' and 'Sunside', sharing one address; NOT two separate venues)

identity.notes: The retained agenda page's own <title>/meta description read 'Agenda - Sunset Sunside jazz club Paris 1er' at the venue's own domain sunset-sunside.com. Every sampled Events Calendar API record's own nested 'venue' object directly states address '60 rue des Lombards', city 'Paris 1er', zip '75001' — matching this investigation's assigned address exactly — under TWO distinct room names, 'Sunset' and 'Sunside', confirming the task's own one-venue-two-rooms model rather than two separate venues.
